english.title: Obstruct constable in enforcement of justices closure order
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), intentionally obstructed a constable from entering premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), which was subject to a closure order made by **(..SPECIFY THE COURT..) Magistrates' Court on **(..SPECIFY THE DATE OF ISSUE..) and having so entered, from doing anything reasonably necessary for the purpose of securing compliance with the order, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OBSTRUCTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 25(3) of the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
intentionally obstructed a constable from entering premises
which was subject to a closure order made by a magistrates' court
and having so entered from doing anything reasonably necessary
for the purpose of securing compliance with the order

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) In section 25 an "authorised person" means a person authorised for the purposes of that Section by a local authority in respect of premises situated in the area of that local authority
(ii) See section 28 for the meaning of "closure order", "premises" and "local authority".
(iii) This does NOT apply to liquor licensed premises.

other.penalty:
One month imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
